process_area.title: Political Engagement Policy, Governance & Risk Assessment

value_stream.name: Corporate Political Engagement, Election Compliance & Public Affairs Governance

fields.Owner: VP Legal & Compliance / Chief Compliance Officer
fields.Participants: Legal (links to VS-100), Compliance (links to VS-119), Govt Affairs (links to VS-104), Finance (links to VS-17.4), Corporate Communications (links to VS-14.3), Board (links to VS-36), ABC (links to VS-86)
fields.Trigger: Program stand-up; annual review; regulatory/election cycle

workflows.name: Corporate Political Engagement Policy, Governance & Operating Model

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "accountable, non-partisan-by-default, transparent" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-record of "VP Legal establish governance" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "approve budget/resourcing, and cascade as a board-level risk" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: dedicated program and policy; operational: clear principles and prohibitions
Pain Points / Risks: - **No-owner risk**: Political activity governed ad-hoc; mitigated by dedicated program and policy
- **Policy-ambiguity risk**: Unclear what's permitted; mitigated by clear principles and prohibitions
System Touchpoints: - Governance (links to VS-36); legal (links to VS-100); govt affairs (links to VS-104); ABC (links to VS-86); ethics (links to VS-119); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: VP Legal & Compliance define the political-engagement policy: principles (lawful, accountable, non-partisan-by-default, transparent), the relationship to ABC (VS-86), government affairs (VS-104), ethics (VS-119), and B2G sales (VS-46); and the prohibitions (corporate contributions to candidates/parties largely prohibited under the Omnibus Election Code and RA 9006)

VP Legal establish governance: a political-engagement oversight (Board Audit/Risk Committee), an approval authority for any political-adjacent spend/activity, decision rights, and integration with records (VS-88), disclosure (W4032), and speak-up (VS-119)
CEO/Board ratify the policy, approve budget/resourcing, and cascade as a board-level risk (links to VS-21.2 ERM and VS-36 governance)

fields.Participants: Legal, Govt Affairs (links to VS-104), Insights (links to VS-44), Compliance (links to VS-119), Strategy (links to VS-33), affected regions
fields.Trigger: Annual; election cycle; major policy issue; new region/LGU

workflows.name: Political Activity Risk Assessment & Stakeholder / Issue Mapping

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-issue of "issues material to BuildRight" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-identify of "identify prohibited/high-risk activities, and set the engagement guardrails" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "document the assessment, feed it into the engagement plan" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-626 (ensure controlled execution — Political Engagement Policy, Governance & Risk Assessment (PA-132.1).)
- operational: monitoring (links to W4040); operational: guardrails
Pain Points / Risks: - **Blind-spot risk**: Material political/regulatory change missed; mitigated by monitoring (links to W4040)
- **Over-engagement risk**: Activity crossing into prohibited partisanship; mitigated by guardrails
System Touchpoints: - Govt affairs (links to VS-104); insights (links to VS-44); strategy (links to VS-33); LGU (links to VS-76); B2G (links to VS-46); ERM (links to VS-21.2)

steps.activity: Govt Affairs/Legal map political stakeholders (national, regional, LGU, regulators) and policy issues material to BuildRight (retail tax/e-invoicing, consumer, labor, customs/tariff, energy, data privacy, property/lease), and assess the political/regulatory risk landscape

Legal/Compliance assess political-activity risk by region/entity (election cycles, hot-button issues, sensitivity of LGU relationships links to VS-76, B2G exposure links to VS-46), identify prohibited/high-risk activities, and set the engagement guardrails
Govt Affairs/Legal document the assessment, feed it into the engagement plan (links to VS-104) and the election-period protocol (W4033), and refresh on cycle/change

fields.Participants: Legal, Finance (links to VS-17.4), Compliance (links to VS-119), ABC (links to VS-86), Govt Affairs (links to VS-104), CEO, Board
fields.Trigger: Contribution/donation request; spend decision; disclosure cycle

workflows.name: Political Contribution & Donation Policy, Approval & Disclosure

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "Legal/Finance maintain the political-contribution/donation policy" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "review every request or spend that could be construed as political" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-record of "record and disclose any permitted political-adjacent spend" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: prohibition, review, and Board authority; operational: nexus review and anti-graft controls
Pain Points / Risks: - **Prohibited-contribution risk**: Corporate funds reaching a candidate/party (criminal liability); mitigated by prohibition, review, and Board authority
- **Disguised-contribution risk**: CSR/sponsorship with electoral nexus; mitigated by nexus review and anti-graft controls
System Touchpoints: - Finance (links to VS-17.4); ABC (links to VS-86); ethics (links to VS-119); records (links to VS-88); governance (links to VS-36); CSR (links to VS-25.2)

steps.activity: Legal/Finance maintain the political-contribution/donation policy: the general prohibition on corporate contributions to candidates/parties/election campaigns under the Omnibus Election Code and RA 9006; the narrow permitted categories (lawful CSR/community donations links to VS-25.2 with no electoral nexus); approval authority (Board for any political-adjacent spend); and documentation/disclosure requirements

Legal/Compliance review every request or spend that could be construed as political (sponsorships of political events, donations to political foundations, in-kind support, candidate-linked charity), apply the ABC controls (links to VS-86) and anti-graft controls (links to W4037), and route to approval or decline
Finance/Legal record and disclose any permitted political-adjacent spend (links to W4032 and VS-17.4), and report to the Board Audit Committee (links to VS-36)

fields.Participants: Govt Affairs (links to VS-104), Legal (links to VS-100), Compliance (links to VS-119), Corporate Communications (links to VS-14.3), Strategy (links to VS-33)
fields.Trigger: Advocacy activity; lobbying engagement; disclosure cycle

workflows.name: Lobbying, Advocacy & Public-Affairs Activity Governance & Disclosure

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "documentation requirements, the conduct standards" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-log of "log all lobbying/advocacy engagements" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-generate of "prepare lobbying/advocacy disclosure" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: registry and disclosure; operational: conduct standards and ABC controls
Pain Points / Risks: - **Undisclosed-lobbying risk**: Engagements not logged; mitigated by registry and disclosure
- **Conduct-breach risk**: Advocacy crossing into improper inducement; mitigated by conduct standards and ABC controls
System Touchpoints: - Govt affairs (links to VS-104); legal (links to VS-100); ABC/anti-graft (links to VS-86); competition (links to VS-129); records (links to VS-88); governance (links to VS-36)

steps.activity: Govt Affairs/Legal govern lobbying and advocacy activity (within VS-104): define what constitutes lobbying/advocacy, the approval and documentation requirements, the conduct standards (truthful, no improper inducements links to VS-86), and any registration/disclosure obligations (Philippine context and any foreign registration where BuildRight's B2B/export activity triggers it)

Govt Affairs/Compliance log all lobbying/advocacy engagements (official met, topic, position, outcome), maintain a single registry, and ensure conduct aligns with anti-graft (links to W4037) and competition guardrails (links to VS-129 W3965 association protocol)
Govt Affairs/Legal prepare lobbying/advocacy disclosure (links to W4032) and report activity to the Board (links to VS-36)

fields.Participants: Govt Affairs (links to VS-104), Legal, Compliance (links to VS-119), Sustainability (links to VS-25), affected business units
fields.Trigger: Membership renewal; advocacy-position misalignment; annual review

workflows.name: Trade Association, Industry-Body & Third-Party Advocacy Membership Review

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "review all trade-association, industry-body, coalition, and…" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "document the rationale" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report membership decisions to the Board" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-626 (ensure controlled execution — Political Engagement Policy, Governance & Risk Assessment (PA-132.1).)
- operational: review and objection/exit; operational: disclosure
Pain Points / Risks: - **Misattribution risk**: BuildRight associated with a body's objectionable position; mitigated by review and objection/exit
- **Undisclosed-influence risk**: Memberships funding undisclosed advocacy; mitigated by disclosure
System Touchpoints: - Govt affairs (links to VS-104); legal (links to VS-100); competition (links to VS-129); ESG (links to VS-25); records (links to VS-88); governance (links to VS-36)

steps.activity: Govt Affairs/Legal review all trade-association, industry-body, coalition, and third-party-advocacy memberships (links to VS-104.2): dues, the positions advocated on BuildRight's behalf, alignment with BuildRight policy/ethics, and any political/election activity by the body

Govt Affairs/Compliance assess misalignment risk (a body advocating positions BuildRight disagrees with or that create reputational/competition risk links to VS-129), decide on continued membership or objection, and document the rationale
Govt Affairs disclose material memberships/dues (links to W4032) and report membership decisions to the Board (links to VS-36)

fields.Participants: HR (links to VS-19/VS-103), Legal (links to VS-100), Compliance (links to VS-119), Labor Relations (links to VS-84), Communications (links to VS-103.1)

workflows.name: Employee Political Activity, Time-Off & Non-Coercion Governance

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-communication of "communicate the policy to employees" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: non-coercion policy and speak-up; operational: rules and oversight
Pain Points / Risks: - **Coercion risk**: Managers pressuring staff politically; mitigated by non-coercion policy and speak-up
- **Resource-misuse risk**: Company resources used for partisanship; mitigated by rules and oversight
System Touchpoints: - HR (links to VS-19/VS-103); labor relations (links to VS-84); ethics (links to VS-119); comms (links to VS-103.1); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: HR/Legal establish employee political-activity governance: employees' personal right to participate politically on their own time, the prohibition on coercion (no pressure to support candidates/parties/positions), rules on company-time/company-resource political activity, and any lawful time-off for voting/civic duties

HR/Compliance manage company-organized political activity (rare/none by default), ensure no BuildRight resources are used for partisan purposes, and address any coercion concerns via speak-up (links to VS-119)
HR/Legal communicate the policy to employees (links to VS-103.1), train managers, and handle questions/incidents (links to VS-119)

fields.Participants: Legal, Govt Affairs (links to VS-104), Procurement (links to VS-34), Compliance (links to VS-119/VS-86), Finance (links to VS-17.4)
fields.Trigger: Engagement of political-affairs consultant/lobbyist; vendor spend; PAC question

workflows.name: Political-Engagement Vendor, Consultant & PAC (if any) Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-record of "Legal/Finance manage vendor payments, retain records" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-626 (ensure controlled execution — Political Engagement Policy, Governance & Risk Assessment (PA-132.1).)
- operational: DD and conduct standards; operational: prohibition and Board clearance
Pain Points / Risks: - **Rogue-vendor risk**: Consultant acting improperly on BuildRight's behalf; mitigated by DD and conduct standards
- **PAC-exposure risk**: Improper political fund; mitigated by prohibition and Board clearance
System Touchpoints: - Procurement (links to VS-34); ABC (links to VS-86); ethics (links to VS-119); finance (links to VS-17.4); legal (links to VS-100); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: Legal/Govt-Affairs govern political-affairs consultants, lobbyists, and public-affairs vendors: due diligence (links to VS-86 ABC screening), scope/engagement letters, conduct standards (no improper inducements, disclosure), and procurement controls (links to VS-34)

Legal/Compliance assess any BuildRight-affiliated political action committee (PAC) or employee-funded political fund (generally not applicable / prohibited in the Philippine context), and ensure none is established or operated without Board approval and legal clearance
Legal/Finance manage vendor payments, retain records (links to VS-88), and disclose (links to W4032) any political-affairs vendor spend

fields.Participants: Legal, Compliance, Govt Affairs (links to VS-104), Finance (links to VS-17.4), Sustainability/ESG (links to VS-25.3), Corporate Communications (links to VS-14.3)

workflows.name: Political Engagement Records, Transparency & Public Disclosure

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-record of "Legal/Compliance maintain the political-engagement records registry" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-generate of "prepare political-engagement transparency disclosure" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-626 (ensure controlled execution — Political Engagement Policy, Governance & Risk Assessment (PA-132.1).)
- operational: registry and approval gates; operational: accuracy
Pain Points / Risks: - **Incomplete-record risk**: Spend/activity not captured; mitigated by registry and approval gates
- **Greenwashing-equivalent risk**: Disclosure overstating restraint; mitigated by accuracy
System Touchpoints: - Records (links to VS-88); ESG/reporting (links to VS-25.3); comms (links to VS-14.3); governance (links to VS-36); finance (links to VS-17.4)

steps.activity: Legal/Compliance maintain the political-engagement records registry: contributions/donations (permitted), lobbying/advocacy engagements, association memberships/dues, political-affairs vendor spend, and any political-adjacent spend — with documentation and approval evidence (links to VS-88)

Legal/Sustainability prepare political-engagement transparency disclosure (integrated into ESG/sustainability reporting links to VS-25.3 or a standalone statement): political contributions (none/prohibited), lobbying/advocacy positions, association memberships, and governance
Legal/Comms manage disclosure risk (sensitivity, accuracy), publish, and respond to stakeholder/investor/lender queries (links to W4021-equivalent stakeholder engagement and VS-14.3)
